features.name: Rage
features.desc:
In battle, you fight with primal ferocity. On your turn, you can enter a rage as a bonus action. While raging, you gain the following benefits if you aren't wearing heavy armor:
- You have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.
- When you make a melee weapon Attack using Strength, you gain a +2 bonus to the damage roll. This bonus increases as you level.
- You have Resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.
If you are able to cast Spells, you can't cast them or concentrate on them while raging.
Your rage lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if you are knocked Unconscious or if Your Turn ends and you haven't attacked a hostile creature since your last turn or taken damage since then. You can also end your rage on Your Turn as a Bonus Action.
Once you have raged the maximum number of times for your barbarian level, you must finish a Long Rest before you can rage again. You may rage 2 times at 1st level, 3 at 3rd, 4 at 6th, 5 at 12th, and 6 at 17th.
features.summary: Bonus action to rage for 1 minute unless in heavy armor: advantage on Str checks/saves, bonus melee Str damage per Rage Damage column, resistance to bludgeoning/piercing/slashing. No spellcasting or concentration. Ends early if unconscious or no attack/damage since last turn.

features.name: Unarmored Defense
features.desc: While you are not wearing any armor, your Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit.
features.summary: With no armor worn, AC is 10 + Dex mod + Con mod; a shield may still be used.

features.name: Reckless Attack
features.desc: Starting at 2nd level, you can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with fierce desperation. When you make your first attack on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you advantage on melee weapon attack rolls using Strength during this turn, but attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.
features.summary: On your first attack of the turn, choose to gain advantage on Str-based melee weapon attacks this turn; attacks against you have advantage until your next turn.

features.name: Danger Sense
features.desc: At 2nd level, you gain an uncanny sense of when things nearby aren't as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge away from danger. You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws against effects that you can see, such as traps and spells. To gain this benefit, you can't be blinded, deafened, or incapacitated.
features.summary: Advantage on Dex saves against effects you can see (traps, spells), provided you are not blinded, deafened, or incapacitated.

features.name: Primal Path
features.desc: At 3rd level, you choose a path that shapes the nature of your rage. Choose the Path of the Berserker or the Path of the Totem Warrior, both detailed at the end of the class description. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th levels.
features.summary: Pick a path (Berserker or Totem Warrior) that grants features at 3rd, 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
features.summary: At 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, add +2 to one ability or +1 to two abilities, max 20.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.desc: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
features.summary: Make two attacks instead of one when taking the Attack action.

features.name: Fast Movement
features.desc: Starting at 5th level, your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing heavy armor.
features.summary: +10 ft. walking speed while not in heavy armor.

features.name: Feral Instinct
features.desc:
By 7th level, your instincts are so honed that you have advantage on initiative rolls.
Additionally, if you are surprised at the beginning of combat and aren't incapacitated, you can act normally on your first turn, but only if you enter your rage before doing anything else on that turn.
features.summary: Advantage on initiative. If surprised and not incapacitated, you may act on your first turn as long as you rage before doing anything else.

features.name: Brutal Critical
features.desc: Beginning at 9th level, you can roll one additional weapon damage die when determining the extra damage for a critical hit with a melee attack. This increases to two additional dice at 13th level and three additional dice at 17th level.
features.summary: Roll one extra weapon damage die on melee critical hits; two extra dice at 13th level, three at 17th.

features.name: Relentless Rage
features.desc:
Starting at 11th level, your rage can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 hit points while you're raging and don't die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw. If you succeed, you drop to 1 hit point instead.
Each time you use this feature after the first, the DC increases by 5. When you finish a short or long rest, the DC resets to 10.
features.summary: When dropped to 0 HP while raging (not killed outright), DC 10 Con save to stay at 1 HP instead. DC rises by 5 per later use; resets on a short or long rest.

features.name: Persistent Rage
features.desc: Beginning at 15th level, your rage is so fierce that it ends early only if you fall unconscious or if you choose to end it.
features.summary: Rage only ends early if you fall unconscious or choose to end it.

features.name: Indomitable Might
features.desc: Beginning at 18th level, if your total for a Strength check is less than your Strength score, you can use that score in place of the total.
features.summary: If a Strength check total is below your Strength score, use the score instead.

features.name: Primal Champion
features.desc: At 20th level, you embody the power of the wilds. Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by 4. Your maximum for those scores is now 24.
features.summary: Strength and Constitution each rise by 4, and their maximum becomes 24.

features.name: Frenzy
features.desc: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, you can go into a frenzy when you rage. If you do so, for the duration of your rage you can make a single melee weapon attack as a bonus action on each of your turns after this one. When your rage ends, you suffer one level of exhaustion (as described in appendix A).
features.summary: When you rage you may frenzy: one melee weapon attack as a bonus action each turn after this one; gain one level of exhaustion when the rage ends.

features.name: Mindless Rage
features.desc: Beginning at 6th level, you can't be charmed or frightened while raging. If you are charmed or frightened when you enter your rage, the effect is suspended for the duration of the rage.
features.summary: Immune to charmed and frightened while raging; such existing effects are suspended during the rage.

features.name: Intimidating Presence
features.desc:
Beginning at 10th level, you can use your action to frighten someone with your menacing presence. When you do so, choose one creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. If the creature can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier) or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn. On subsequent turns, you can use your action to extend the duration of this effect on the frightened creature until the end of your next turn. This effect ends if the creature ends its turn out of line of sight or more than 60 feet away from you.
 If the creature succeeds on its saving throw, you can't use this feature on that creature again for 24 hours.
features.summary: Action: one creature within 30 ft. that can see/hear you makes a Wis save (DC 8 + prof + Cha) or is frightened until end of your next turn; extend with your action each turn. Ends beyond 60 ft. or out of sight. On a success, that creature is immune for 24 hours.

features.name: Retaliation
features.desc: Starting at 14th level, when you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon Attack against that creature.
features.summary: Reaction when a creature within 5 ft. damages you: make one melee weapon attack against it.

features.name: Spirit Seeker
features.summary: Can cast beast sense and speak with animals, but only as rituals.

features.name: Totem Spirit
features.summary: Choose a totem animal (Bear, Eagle, or Wolf) and gain its rage benefit; requires a physical totem object incorporating parts of that animal.

features.name: Aspect of the Beast
features.summary: Choose a totem animal (same or different) and gain its always-on benefit: Bear, Eagle, or Wolf.

features.name: Spirit Walker
features.summary: Can cast commune with nature, but only as a ritual; a spirit of one of your chosen totem animals delivers the information.

features.name: Totemic Attunement
features.summary: Choose a totem animal (same or different) and gain its rage benefit: Bear, Eagle, or Wolf.

choices.name: Bear
choices.summary: While raging, resistance to every damage type except psychic.

choices.name: Eagle
choices.summary: While raging and not in heavy armor, opportunity attacks against you have disadvantage and you can Dash as a bonus action.

choices.name: Wolf
choices.summary: While raging, allies have advantage on melee attacks against hostile creatures within 5 ft. of you.

choices.name: Bear
choices.summary: Carrying capacity (incl. max load and lift) doubled; advantage on Str checks to push, pull, lift, or break.

choices.name: Eagle
choices.summary: See up to 1 mile clearly, discerning fine detail as if within 100 ft.; dim light does not impose disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks.

choices.name: Wolf
choices.summary: Track creatures while traveling at a fast pace, and move stealthily at a normal pace.

choices.name: Bear
choices.summary: While raging, hostile creatures within 5 ft. have disadvantage on attacks against anyone but you or others with this feature (unless they can't see/hear you or can't be frightened).

choices.name: Eagle
choices.summary: While raging, gain a flying speed equal to walking speed, but you fall if you end your turn airborne with nothing holding you up.

choices.name: Wolf
choices.summary: While raging, when you hit a Large or smaller creature with a melee weapon attack, bonus action to knock it prone.

startingEquipmentOptions.desc: (a) a greataxe or (b) any martial melee weapon

name: Bard
proficiencies: Three musical instruments of your choice

features.name: Spellcasting
features.desc: You have learned to untangle and reshape the fabric of reality in harmony with your wishes and music. Your spells are part of your vast repertoire, magic that you can tune to different situations.
features.summary: Known-spells Cha caster from the bard list (cantrips and spells known per table); swap one known spell on level-up; can ritual-cast known ritual spells; musical instrument as focus. Save DC 8 + prof + Cha.

features.name: Bardic Inspiration
features.desc:
You can inspire others through stirring words or music. To do so, you use a bonus action on your turn to choose one creature other than yourself within 60 feet of you who can hear you. That creature gains one Bardic Inspiration die, a d6. Once within the next 10 minutes, the creature can roll the die and add the number rolled to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw it makes. The creature can wait until after it rolls the d20 before deciding to use the Bardic Inspiration die, but must decide before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails. Once the Bardic Inspiration die is rolled, it is lost. A creature can have only one Bardic Inspiration die at a time.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once). You regain any expended uses when you finish a long rest. 
Your Bardic Inspiration die changes when you reach certain levels in this class. The die becomes a d8 at 5th level, a d10 at 10th level, and a d12 at 15th level.
features.summary: Bonus action: give a creature (not you) within 60 ft. that can hear you an inspiration die (d6, d8 at 5th, d10 at 10th, d12 at 15th) to add to one ability check, attack, or save within 10 minutes. One die per creature.

features.name: Jack of All Trades
features.desc: Starting at 2nd level, you can add half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, to any ability check you make that doesn't already include your proficiency bonus.
features.summary: Add half proficiency bonus (rounded down) to any ability check that doesn't already use your proficiency bonus.

features.name: Song of Rest
features.desc:
Beginning at 2nd level, you can use soothing music or oration to help revitalize your wounded allies during a short rest. If you or any friendly creatures who can hear your performance regain hit points at the end of the short rest by spending one or more Hit Dice, each of those creatures regains an extra 1d6 hit points. 
The extra hit points increase when you reach certain levels in this class: to 1d8 at 9th level, to 1d10 at 13th level, and to 1d12 at 17th level.
features.summary: During a short rest, you and friendly listeners who spend Hit Dice regain extra 1d6 HP (1d8 at 9th, 1d10 at 13th, 1d12 at 17th).

features.name: Bard College
features.desc: At 3rd level, you delve into the advanced techniques of a bard college of your choice, such as the College of Lore. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th and 14th level.
features.summary: Choose College of Lore or College of Valor, granting features at 3rd, 6th, and 14th level.

features.name: Expertise
features.desc: At 3rd level, choose two of your skill proficiencies. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies. At 10th level, you can choose another two skill proficiencies to gain this benefit.
features.summary: Double proficiency bonus for two chosen skill proficiencies; pick two more at 10th level.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
features.summary: At 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, add +2 to one ability or +1 to two abilities, max 20.

features.name: Font of Inspiration
features.desc: Beginning when you reach 5th level, you regain all of your expended uses of Bardic Inspiration when you finish a short or long rest.
features.summary: Bardic Inspiration uses now recover on a short or long rest.

features.name: Countercharm
features.desc: At 6th level, you gain the ability to use musical notes or words of power to disrupt mind-influencing effects. As an action, you can start a performance that lasts until the end of your next turn. During that time, you and any friendly creatures within 30 feet of you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened or charmed. A creature must be able to hear you to gain this benefit. The performance ends early if you are incapacitated or silenced or if you voluntarily end it (no action required).
features.summary: Action: perform until end of next turn; you and friendly creatures within 30 ft. that can hear you have advantage on saves against frightened and charmed. Ends if incapacitated, silenced, or you stop.

features.name: Magical Secrets
features.desc:
By 10th level, you have plundered magical knowledge from a wide spectrum of disciplines. Choose two spells from any class, including this one. A spell you choose must be of a level you can cast, as shown on the Bard table, or a cantrip. 
The chosen spells count as bard spells for you and are included in the number in the Spells Known column of the Bard table. 
You learn two additional spells from any class at 14th level and again at 18th level.
features.summary: Learn two spells of any class (of a level you can cast, or cantrips); they count as bard spells and toward Spells Known. Two more at 14th and 18th.

features.name: Superior Inspiration
features.desc: At 20th level, when you roll initiative and have no uses of Bardic Inspiration left, you regain one use.
features.summary: When you roll initiative with no Bardic Inspiration uses left, regain one use.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.desc: When you join the College of Lore at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.
features.summary: Gain proficiency in three skills of your choice.

features.name: Cutting Words
features.desc:
Also at 3rd level, you learn how to use your wit to distract, confuse, and otherwise sap the confidence and competence of others.
When a creature that you can see within 60 feet of you makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a damage roll, you can use your reaction to expend one of your uses of Bardic Inspiration, rolling a Bardic Inspiration die and subtracting the number rolled from the creature's roll.
You can choose to use this feature after the creature makes its roll, but before the GM determines whether the attack roll or ability check succeeds or fails, or before the creature deals its damage. The creature is immune if it can't hear you or if it's immune to being charmed.
features.summary: Reaction: when a creature within 60 ft. you can see makes an attack roll, ability check, or damage roll, spend a Bardic Inspiration use and subtract the die from its roll. Creatures that can't hear you or can't be charmed are immune.

features.name: Additional Magical Secrets
features.desc: At 6th level, you learn two spells of your choice from any class. A spell you choose must be of a level you can cast, as shown on the Bard table, or a cantrip. The chosen spells count as bard spells for you but don't count against the number of bard spells you know.
features.summary: Learn two spells from any class (castable level or cantrip); they count as bard spells but not against Spells Known.

features.name: Peerless Skill
features.desc: Starting at 14th level, when you make an ability check, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration. Roll a Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to your ability check. You can choose to do so after you roll the die for the ability check, but before the GM tells you whether you succeed or fail.
features.summary: Spend a Bardic Inspiration use to add the die to your own ability check, deciding after the roll but before the outcome is known.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.summary: Gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and martial weapons.

features.name: Combat Inspiration
features.summary: A creature holding your Bardic Inspiration die may add it to a weapon damage roll it just made, or use its reaction to add it to AC against an attack after seeing the roll.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.summary: Make two attacks instead of one when taking the Attack action.

features.name: Battle Magic
features.summary: After using your action to cast a bard spell, make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

startingEquipmentOptions.desc: (a) a rapier, (b) a longsword, or (c) any simple weapon
(a) a diplomat’s pack or (b) an entertainer’s pack
(a) a lute or (b) any other musical instrument

features.name: Spellcasting
features.desc: As a conduit for divine power, you can cast cleric spells.
features.summary: Full Wisdom caster that prepares spells daily from the whole cleric list (Wis mod + cleric level, min 1). Can ritual-cast prepared ritual spells; holy symbol works as focus.

features.name: Divine Domain
features.desc:
Choose one domain related to your deity, such as Knowledge, Life, Light, Nature, Tempest, Trickery, or War. Only the Life domain is detailed in the Open Game Licensed SRD. Additional Domains are described in the official rulebooks or products from other publishers.
Your domain grants you domain spells and other features when you choose it at 1st level. It also grants you additional ways to use Channel Divinity when you gain that feature at 2nd level, and additional benefits at 6th, 8th, and 17th levels.
features.summary: Pick a domain tied to your deity (Knowledge, Life, Light, Nature, Tempest, Trickery, War). It grants features at 1st, 2nd (Channel Divinity option), 6th, 8th and 17th level.

features.name: Domain Spells
features.desc:
Each domain has a list of spells--its domain spells--that you gain at the cleric levels noted in the domain description. Once you gain a domain spell, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day.
If you have a domain spell that doesn't appear on the cleric spell list, the spell is nonetheless a cleric spell for you.
features.summary: Your domain adds two spells at cleric levels 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9. They are always prepared, don't count toward your prepared total, and count as cleric spells for you.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.desc:
At 2nd level, you gain the ability to channel divine energy directly from your deity, using that energy to fuel magical effects. You start with two such effects: Turn Undead and an effect determined by your domain. Some domains grant you additional effects as you advance in levels, as noted in the domain description.
When you use your Channel Divinity, you choose which effect to create. You must then finish a short or long rest to use your Channel Divinity again.
Some Channel Divinity effects require saving throws. When you use such an effect from this class, the DC equals your cleric spell save DC.
Beginning at 6th level, you can use your Channel Divinity twice between rests, and beginning at 18th level, you can use it three times between rests. When you finish a short or long rest, you regain your expended uses.
features.summary: Spend a use to create one divine effect: Turn Undead or your domain's option(s). Save DCs use your cleric spell save DC. Uses return on a short or long rest; 2 uses at 6th, 3 at 18th.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Turn Undead
features.desc:
As an action, you present your holy symbol and speak a prayer censuring the undead. Each undead that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. If the creature fails its saving throw, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes any damage.
A turned creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as it can, and it can't willingly move to a space within 30 feet of you. It also can't take reactions. For its action, it can use only the Dash action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving. If there's nowhere to move, the creature can use the Dodge action.
features.summary: Action: undead within 30 ft. that see or hear you make a Wis save; on a failure each is turned for 1 minute or until damaged, fleeing you and unable to take reactions.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
features.summary: At 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th and 19th level, add +2 to one ability or +1 to two abilities (max 20).

features.name: Destroy Undead
features.desc: Starting at 5th level, when an undead fails its saving throw against your Turn Undead feature, the creature is instantly destroyed if its challenge rating is at or below a certain threshold.
features.summary: Undead that fail the save against your Turn Undead are destroyed outright if their CR is at or below the threshold: 1/2 at 5th, 1 at 8th, 2 at 11th, 3 at 14th, 4 at 17th.

features.name: Divine Intervention
features.desc:
Beginning at 10th level, you can call on your deity to intervene on your behalf when your need is great.
Imploring your deity's aid requires you to use your action. Describe the assistance you seek, and roll percentile dice. If you roll a number equal to or lower than your cleric level, your deity intervenes. The GM chooses the nature of the intervention; the effect of any cleric spell or cleric domain spell would be appropriate.
If your deity intervenes, you can't use this feature again for 7 days. Otherwise, you can use it again after you finish a long rest.
At 20th level, your call for intervention succeeds automatically, no roll required.
features.summary: Action: ask your god for help and roll d100; if the roll is no higher than your cleric level the DM grants aid. Success locks it for 7 days, failure until a long rest. Auto-succeeds at 20th.

features.name: Bonus Proficiency
features.desc: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with heavy armor.
features.summary: Gain heavy armor proficiency.

features.name: Disciple of Life
features.desc: Also starting at 1st level, your healing spells are more effective. Whenever you use a spell of 1st level or higher to restore hit points to a creature, the creature regains additional hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.
features.summary: Healing spells of 1st level or higher restore an extra 2 + spell level hit points to each creature they heal.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Preserve Life
features.desc:
Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to heal the badly injured.
As an action, you present your holy symbol and evoke healing energy that can restore a number of hit points equal to five times your cleric level.
Choose any creatures within 30 feet of you, and divide those hit points among them. This feature can restore a creature to no more than half of its hit point maximum. You can't use this feature on an undead or a construct.
features.summary: Action: split 5 x cleric level hit points of healing among creatures within 30 ft., raising none above half its max HP. No effect on undead or constructs.

features.name: Blessed Healer
features.desc: Beginning at 6th level, the healing spells you cast on others heal you as well. When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that restores hit points to a creature other than you, you regain hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.
features.summary: When a 1st-level-or-higher spell of yours heals someone other than you, you also regain 2 + spell level hit points.

features.name: Divine Strike
features.desc: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.
features.summary: Once per turn on a weapon hit, add 1d8 radiant damage (2d8 from 14th level).

features.name: Supreme Healing
features.summary: Healing spell dice are not rolled; each die counts as its maximum value.

features.name: Blessings of Knowledge
features.summary: Learn two languages and gain proficiency in two of Arcana, History, Nature or Religion; your proficiency bonus is doubled for checks with those two skills.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Knowledge of the Ages
features.summary: Action: choose one skill or tool and be proficient with it for 10 minutes.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Read Thoughts
features.summary: Action: a creature within 60 ft. makes a Wis save. On a failure you read its surface thoughts for 1 minute and may end it to cast suggestion on it (no slot, auto-fail). If it saves, you can't retry this until a long rest.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting
features.summary: Add your Wisdom modifier to damage dealt by your cleric cantrips.

features.name: Visions of the Past
features.summary: Meditate (concentration, up to Wis-score minutes) to see past events: Object Reading reveals an item's previous owner(s); Area Reading reveals significant events nearby going back Wis-score days.

choices.name: Object Reading
choices.summary: After 1 minute holding an object, learn how its owner got and lost it and the latest notable event involving them; extra minutes reveal earlier recent owners.

choices.name: Area Reading
choices.summary: Each minute of meditation reveals one significant event in the surrounding area (up to a 50-ft. cube), newest first, going back up to Wis-score days.

features.name: Bonus Cantrip
features.summary: Learn the light cantrip if you don't already know it.

features.name: Warding Flare
features.summary: Reaction when a creature within 30 ft. you can see attacks you: impose disadvantage on that attack (creatures immune to blindness are unaffected).

features.name: Channel Divinity: Radiance of the Dawn
features.summary: Action: dispel magical darkness within 30 ft.; hostile creatures there make a Con save, taking 2d10 + cleric level radiant damage (half on success). Total cover protects.

features.name: Improved Flare
features.summary: Warding Flare can also protect another creature attacked within 30 ft. of you.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting
features.summary: Add your Wisdom modifier to damage dealt by your cleric cantrips.

features.name: Corona of Light
features.summary: Action: emit sunlight (60 ft. bright, 30 ft. more dim) for 1 minute; enemies in the bright light have disadvantage on saves against fire or radiant spells.

features.name: Acolyte of Nature
features.summary: Learn one druid cantrip and gain proficiency in Animal Handling, Nature or Survival (pick one).

features.name: Bonus Proficiency
features.summary: Gain heavy armor proficiency.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Charm Animals and Plants
features.summary: Action: beasts and plant creatures within 30 ft. that see you make a Wis save or are charmed (friendly to you and allies) for 1 minute or until damaged.

features.name: Dampen Elements
features.summary: Reaction: give yourself or a creature within 30 ft. resistance against one instance of acid, cold, fire, lightning or thunder damage.

features.name: Divine Strike
features.summary: Once per turn on a weapon hit, add 1d8 cold, fire or lightning damage (your pick); 2d8 from 14th level.

features.name: Master of Nature
features.summary: Bonus action: command creatures charmed by your Charm Animals and Plants what to do on their next turn.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.summary: Gain martial weapon and heavy armor proficiency.

features.name: Wrath of the Storm
features.summary: Reaction when a creature within 5 ft. that you can see hits you: it makes a Dex save, taking 2d8 lightning or thunder damage (half on success).

features.name: Channel Divinity: Destructive Wrath
features.summary: When you roll lightning or thunder damage, spend Channel Divinity to deal the maximum instead of rolling.

features.name: Thunderbolt Strike
features.summary: When you deal lightning damage to a Large or smaller creature, you can also push it up to 10 ft. away.

features.name: Divine Strike
features.summary: Once per turn on a weapon hit, add 1d8 thunder damage (2d8 from 14th level).

features.name: Stormborn
features.summary: Gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed while not underground or indoors.

features.name: Blessing of the Trickster
features.summary: Action: touch a willing creature other than you to give it advantage on Dex (Stealth) checks for 1 hour or until you use this again.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Invoke Duplicity
features.summary: Action: create an illusory double within 30 ft. for 1 minute (concentration). Bonus action moves it 30 ft. (stay within 120 ft.); you may cast spells from its space and gain advantage on attacks vs. creatures adjacent to both of you.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Cloak of Shadows
features.summary: Action: become invisible until the end of your next turn; attacking or casting a spell ends it.

features.name: Divine Strike
features.summary: Once per turn on a weapon hit, add 1d8 poison damage (2d8 from 14th level).

features.name: Improved Duplicity
features.summary: Invoke Duplicity creates up to four duplicates; one bonus action moves any of them up to 30 ft. each (within 120 ft.).

features.name: Druidic
features.desc: You know Druidic, the secret language of druids. You can speak the language and use it to leave hidden messages. You and others who know this language automatically spot such a message. Others spot the message's presence with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check but can't decipher it without magic.
features.summary: You know the secret druid language and can leave hidden messages in it; others notice such a message with a DC 15 Wis (Perception) check but can't read it without magic.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.desc: Drawing on the divine essence of nature itself, you can cast spells to shape that essence to your will.
features.summary: Full Wisdom caster preparing Wis mod + druid level (min 1) spells daily from the druid list; ritual casting for prepared rituals; druidic focus as spellcasting focus.

features.name: Wild Shape
features.desc:
Starting at 2nd level, you can use your action to magically assume the shape of a beast that you have seen before. You can use this feature twice. You regain expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.
Your druid level determines the beasts you can transform into, as shown in the Beast Shapes table. At 2nd level, for example, you can transform into any beast that has a challenge rating of 1/4 or lower that doesn't have a flying or swimming speed.
You can stay in a beast shape for a number of hours equal to half your druid level (rounded down). You then revert to your normal form unless you expend another use of this feature. You can revert to your normal form earlier by using a bonus action on your turn. You automatically revert if you fall unconscious, drop to 0 hit points, or die.
While you are transformed, the following rules apply:
- Your game statistics are replaced by the statistics of the beast, but you retain your alignment, personality, and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores. You also retain all of your skill and saving throw proficiencies, in addition to gaining those of the creature. If the creature has the same proficiency as you and the bonus in its stat block is higher than yours, use the creature's bonus instead of yours. If the creature has any legendary or lair actions, you can't use them.
- When you transform, you assume the beast's hit points and Hit Dice. When you revert to your normal form, you return to the number of hit points you had before you transformed. However, if you revert as a result of dropping to 0 hit points, any excess damage carries over to your normal form. For example, if you take 10 damage in animal form and have only 1 hit point left, you revert and take 9 damage. As long as the excess damage doesn't reduce your normal form to 0 hit points, you aren't knocked unconscious.
- You can't cast spells, and your ability to speak or take any action that requires hands is limited to the capabilities of your beast form. Transforming doesn't break your concentration on a spell you've already cast, however, or prevent you from taking actions that are part of a spell, such as call lightning, that you've already cast.
- You retain the benefit of any features from your class, race, or other source and can use them if the new form is physically capable of doing so. However, you can't use any of your special senses, such as darkvision, unless your new form also has that sense.
- You choose whether your equipment falls to the ground in your space, merges into your new form, or is worn by it. Worn equipment functions as normal, but the GM decides whether it is practical for the new form to wear a piece of equipment, based on the creature's shape and size. Your equipment doesn't change size or shape to match the new form, and any equipment that the new form can't wear must either fall to the ground or merge with it. Equipment that merges with the form has no effect until you leave the form.
features.summary: Action: turn into a beast you have seen, for up to half your druid level in hours. Max CR 1/4 with no fly/swim speed at 2nd; CR 1/2, no fly at 4th; CR 1 at 8th. You take the beast's HP and stats but keep mental scores and can't cast spells.

features.name: Druid Circle
features.desc: At 2nd level, you choose to identify with a circle of druids, such as the Circle of the Land. Your choice grants you features at 2nd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.
features.summary: Join the Circle of the Land or the Circle of the Moon; the circle grants features at 2nd, 6th, 10th and 14th level.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
features.summary: At 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th and 19th level, add +2 to one ability or +1 to two abilities (max 20).

features.name: Timeless Body
features.desc: Starting at 18th level, the primal magic that you wield causes you to age more slowly. For every 10 years that pass, your body ages only 1 year.
features.summary: You age only one year for every ten that pass.

features.name: Beast Spells
features.desc: Beginning at 18th level, you can cast many of your druid spells in any shape you assume using Wild Shape. You can perform the somatic and verbal components of a druid spell while in a beast shape, but you aren't able to provide material components.
features.summary: You can cast druid spells while in Wild Shape, supplying verbal and somatic components but not material ones.

features.name: Archdruid
features.desc:
At 20th level, you can use your Wild Shape an unlimited number of times.
Additionally, you can ignore the verbal and somatic components of your druid spells, as well as any material components that lack a cost and aren't consumed by a spell. You gain this benefit in both your normal shape and your beast shape from Wild Shape.
features.summary: Wild Shape uses become unlimited, and you can skip verbal, somatic and costless non-consumed material components of druid spells in any form.

features.name: Bonus Cantrip
features.desc: When you choose this circle at 2nd level, you learn one additional druid cantrip of your choice.
features.summary: Learn one extra druid cantrip of your choice.

features.name: Natural Recovery
features.desc:
Starting at 2nd level, you can regain some of your magical energy by sitting in meditation and communing with nature. During a short rest, you choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your druid level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher. You can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.
For example, when you are a 4th-level druid, you can recover up to two levels worth of spell slots. You can recover either a 2nd-level slot or two 1st-level slots.
features.summary: During a short rest, recover expended spell slots with a combined level up to half your druid level (rounded up); no slot of 6th level or higher.

features.name: Circle Spells
features.desc:
Your mystical connection to the land infuses you with the ability to cast certain spells. At 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 9th level you gain access to circle spells connected to the land where you became a druid.
Choose that land--arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, or swamp--and consult the associated list of spells.
Once you gain access to a circle spell, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn't appear on the druid spell list, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you.
features.summary: Choose the land you were initiated in; gain its two circle spells at druid levels 3, 5, 7 and 9. They are always prepared, don't count against prepared spells and count as druid spells.

features.name: Land's Stride
features.desc:
Starting at 6th level, moving through nonmagical difficult terrain costs you no extra movement. You can also pass through nonmagical plants without being slowed by them and without taking damage from them if they have thorns, spines, or a similar hazard.
In addition, you have advantage on saving throws against plants that are magically created or manipulated to impede movement, such those created by the entangle spell.
features.summary: Nonmagical difficult terrain costs no extra movement; pass through nonmagical plants unslowed and unharmed; advantage on saves against magical plants that hinder movement (e.g. entangle).

features.name: Nature's Ward
features.desc: When you reach 10th level, you can't be charmed or frightened by elementals or fey, and you are immune to poison and disease.
features.summary: Elementals and fey can't charm or frighten you, and you are immune to poison and disease.

features.name: Nature's Sanctuary
features.desc: When you reach 14th level, creatures of the natural world sense your connection to nature and become hesitant to attack you. When a beast or plant creature attacks you, that creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your druid spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature must choose a different target, or the attack automatically misses. On a successful save, the creature is immune to this effect for 24 hours. The creature is aware of this effect before it makes its attack against you.
features.summary: A beast or plant attacking you must pass a Wis save vs. your spell DC or pick another target (or miss). On a success it is immune for 24 hours; it knows of this effect beforehand.

features.name: Fighting Style
features.desc: You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.
features.summary: Pick one fighting style option (see options); the same style can never be taken twice, even when another choice is granted later.

features.name: Second Wind
features.desc: You have a limited well of stamina that you can draw on to protect yourself from harm. On your turn, you can use a bonus action to regain hit points equal to 1d10 + your fighter level. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.
features.summary: Bonus action on your turn: heal 1d10 + fighter level hit points. Usable once per short or long rest.

features.name: Action Surge
features.desc:
Starting at 2nd level, you can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action on top of your regular action and a possible bonus action.
Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again. Starting at 17th level, you can use it twice before a rest, but only once on the same turn.
features.summary: On your turn, take one extra action. Recharges on a short or long rest; from 17th level two uses per rest, but never twice in one turn.

features.name: Martial Archetype
features.desc: At 3rd level, you choose an archetype that you strive to emulate in your combat styles and techniques, such as Champion. The archetype you choose grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 10th, 15th, and 18th level.
features.summary: Choose Champion, Battle Master or Eldritch Knight; the archetype grants features at 3rd, 7th, 10th, 15th and 18th level.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 6th, 8th, 12th, 14th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
features.summary: At 4th, 6th, 8th, 12th, 14th, 16th and 19th level: +2 to one ability score or +1 to two, to a maximum of 20.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.desc: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. The number of attacks increases to three when you reach 11th level in this class and to four when you reach 20th level in this class.
features.summary: The Attack action lets you attack twice; three attacks from 11th fighter level and four from 20th.

features.name: Indomitable
features.desc: Beginning at 9th level, you can reroll a saving throw that you fail. If you do so, you must use the new roll, and you can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest. You can use this feature twice between long rests starting at 13th level and three times between long rests starting at 17th level.
features.summary: Reroll a failed saving throw and keep the new result. Once per long rest; twice from 13th level, three times from 17th.

features.name: Improved Critical
features.desc: Beginning when you choose this archetype at 3rd level, your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.
features.summary: Weapon attacks crit on a 19 or 20.

features.name: Remarkable Athlete
features.desc: Starting at 7th level, you can add half your proficiency bonus (round up) to any Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution check you make that doesn't already use your proficiency bonus. In addition, when you make a running long jump, the distance you can cover increases by a number of feet equal to your Strength modifier.
features.summary: Add half proficiency bonus (rounded up) to Str, Dex and Con checks that don't already use proficiency; running long jumps gain feet equal to your Strength modifier.

features.name: Additional Fighting Style
features.desc: At 10th level, you can choose a second option from the Fighting Style class feature.
features.summary: Choose a second Fighting Style option.

features.name: Superior Critical
features.desc: Starting at 15th level, your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 18-20.
features.summary: Weapon attacks crit on 18-20.

features.name: Survivor
features.desc: At 18th level, you attain the pinnacle of resilience in battle. At the start of each of your turns, you regain hit points equal to 5 + your Constitution modifier if you have no more than half of your hit points left. You don't gain this benefit if you have 0 hit points.
features.summary: At the start of each turn, if at or below half hit points (but above 0), regain 5 + Constitution modifier hit points.

features.name: Combat Superiority
features.summary: Learn 3 maneuvers (2 more at 7th, 10th and 15th; may swap one each time) fueled by superiority dice: 4d8, +1 die at 7th and 15th, regained on a short or long rest. One maneuver per attack; save DC 8 + prof + Str or Dex modifier.

features.summary: Gain proficiency with one type of artisan's tools of your choice.

features.name: Know Your Enemy
features.summary: After 1 minute observing or interacting with a creature out of combat, learn whether it is your equal, superior or inferior in two chosen traits (Str, Dex, Con, AC, current HP, total class levels, fighter levels).

features.name: Improved Combat Superiority
features.summary: Superiority dice become d10s; at 18th level they become d12s.

features.name: Relentless
features.summary: When you roll initiative with no superiority dice left, regain one.

choices.name: Commander's Strike
choices.summary: Give up one of your Attack-action attacks and use a bonus action plus a die: an ally who can see or hear you uses its reaction to make a weapon attack, adding the die to damage.

choices.name: Disarming Attack
choices.summary: On a weapon hit, add the die to damage; target makes a Strength save or drops an item of your choice at its feet.

choices.name: Distracting Strike
choices.summary: On a weapon hit, add the die to damage; the next attack by someone other than you against that target before your next turn has advantage.

choices.name: Evasive Footwork
choices.summary: While moving, spend a die and add the roll to your AC until you stop moving.

choices.name: Feinting Attack
choices.summary: Bonus action plus a die to feint a creature within 5 feet: advantage on your next attack against it this turn, adding the die to damage if it hits.

choices.name: Goading Attack
choices.summary: On a weapon hit, add the die to damage; target makes a Wisdom save or has disadvantage on attacks against anyone but you until the end of your next turn.

choices.name: Lunging Attack
choices.summary: On a melee weapon attack on your turn, spend a die to gain 5 extra feet of reach for that attack; add the die to damage on a hit.

choices.name: Maneuvering Attack
choices.summary: On a weapon hit, add the die to damage; an ally who can see or hear you may use its reaction to move half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks from the target.

choices.name: Menacing Attack
choices.summary: On a weapon hit, add the die to damage; target makes a Wisdom save or is frightened of you until the end of your next turn.

choices.name: Parry
choices.summary: Reaction when a melee attack damages you: reduce the damage by the die roll + your Dexterity modifier.

choices.name: Precision Attack
choices.summary: Add the die to a weapon attack roll, before or after rolling but before effects are applied.

choices.name: Pushing Attack
choices.summary: On a weapon hit, add the die to damage; a Large or smaller target makes a Strength save or is pushed up to 15 feet away.

choices.name: Rally
choices.summary: Bonus action plus a die: an ally who can see or hear you gains temporary hit points equal to the die roll + your Charisma modifier.

choices.name: Riposte
choices.summary: Reaction when a creature misses you with a melee attack: make one melee weapon attack against it, adding the die to damage on a hit.

choices.name: Sweeping Attack
choices.summary: On a melee weapon hit, choose a second creature within 5 feet of the target and within reach; if the original roll would hit it, it takes the die roll as damage of the same type.

choices.name: Trip Attack
choices.summary: On a weapon hit, add the die to damage; a Large or smaller target makes a Strength save or is knocked prone.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.summary: Cast wizard spells using Intelligence (see spellcasting table). Spells known must be abjuration or evocation, except the ones learned at 3rd (one of the first three), 8th, 14th and 20th level; slots regained on a long rest.

features.name: Weapon Bond
features.summary: A 1-hour ritual bonds up to two weapons to you; a bonded weapon can't be disarmed unless you are incapacitated and can be summoned to your hand as a bonus action on the same plane.

features.name: War Magic
features.summary: After using your action to cast a cantrip, you may make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

features.name: Eldritch Strike
features.summary: A creature you hit with a weapon attack has disadvantage on its next save against a spell you cast before the end of your next turn.

features.name: Arcane Charge
features.summary: When you use Action Surge, you may teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, before or after the extra action.

features.name: Improved War Magic
features.summary: After using your action to cast any spell, you may make one weapon attack as a bonus action.
