features.name: Unarmored Defense
features.desc: Beginning at 1st level, while you are wearing no armor and not wielding a shield, your AC equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Wisdom modifier.
features.summary: With no armor and no shield, AC = 10 + Dex modifier + Wis modifier.

features.name: Martial Arts
features.desc:
At 1st level, your practice of martial arts gives you mastery of combat styles that use unarmed strikes and monk weapons, which are shortswords and any simple melee weapons that don't have the two- handed or heavy property.
You gain the following benefits while you are unarmed or wielding only monk weapons and you aren't wearing armor or wielding a shield:
- You can use Dexterity instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of your unarmed strikes and monk weapons.
- You can roll a d4 in place of the normal damage of your unarmed strike or monk weapon. This die changes as you gain monk levels, as shown in the Martial Arts column of Table: The Monk.
- When you use the Attack action with an unarmed strike or a monk weapon on your turn, you can make one unarmed strike as a bonus action. For example, if you take the Attack action and attack with a quarterstaff, you can also make an unarmed strike as a bonus action, assuming you haven't already taken a bonus action this turn.
Certain monasteries use specialized forms of the monk weapons. For example, you might use a club that is two lengths of wood connected by a short chain (called a nunchaku) or a sickle with a shorter, straighter blade (called a kama). Whatever name you use for a monk weapon, you can use the game statistics provided for the weapon.
features.summary: Unarmed or with monk weapons (shortswords, simple melee weapons without two-handed/heavy) and no armor/shield: use Dex for attack and damage, use the Martial Arts die for damage, and make a bonus-action unarmed strike after attacking with the Attack action.

features.name: Ki
features.desc:
Starting at 2nd level, your training allows you to harness the mystic energy of ki. Your access to this energy is represented by a number of ki points. Your monk level determines the number of points you have, as shown in the Ki Points column of Table: The Monk.
You can spend these points to fuel various ki features. You start knowing three such features: Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind. You learn more ki features as you gain levels in this class.
When you spend a ki point, it is unavailable until you finish a short or long rest, at the end of which you draw all of your expended ki back into yourself. You must spend at least 30 minutes of the rest meditating to regain your ki points.
Some of your ki features require your target to make a saving throw to resist the feature's effects. The saving throw DC is calculated as follows:
Ki save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier
features.summary: Pool of ki points equal to the Ki Points column, regained on a short or long rest with 30 minutes of meditation. Ki save DC = 8 + prof + Wis. Grants Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense and Step of the Wind.

features.name: Flurry of Blows
features.desc: Immediately after you take the Attack action on your turn, you can spend 1 ki point to make two unarmed strikes as a bonus action.
features.summary: Right after the Attack action, spend 1 ki to make two unarmed strikes as a bonus action.

features.name: Patient Defense
features.desc: You can spend 1 ki point to take the Dodge action as a bonus action on your turn.
features.summary: Spend 1 ki to Dodge as a bonus action on your turn.

features.name: Step of the Wind
features.desc: You can spend 1 ki point to take the Disengage or Dash action as a bonus action on your turn, and your jump distance is doubled for the turn.
features.summary: Spend 1 ki to Disengage or Dash as a bonus action; jump distance doubles for the turn.

features.name: Unarmored Movement
features.desc:
Starting at 2nd level, your speed increases by 10 feet while you are not wearing armor or wielding a shield. This bonus increases when you reach certain monk levels, as shown in Table: The Monk.
At 9th level, you gain the ability to move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling during the move.
features.summary: Speed bonus per the Unarmored Movement column while unarmored and without a shield. From 9th level, you can run up vertical surfaces and across liquids during your move.

features.name: Monastic Tradition
features.desc: When you reach 3rd level, you commit yourself to a monastic tradition, such as the Way of the Open Hand. Your tradition grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 11th, and 17th level.
features.summary: Choose Way of the Open Hand, Way of Shadow or Way of the Four Elements; features at 3rd, 6th, 11th and 17th level.

features.name: Deflect Missiles
features.desc:
Starting at 3rd level, you can use your reaction to deflect or catch the missile when you are hit by a ranged weapon attack. When you do so, the damage you take from the attack is reduced by 1d10 + your Dexterity modifier + your monk level.
If you reduce the damage to 0, you can catch the missile if it is small enough for you to hold in one hand and you have at least one hand free. If you catch a missile in this way, you can spend 1 ki point to make a ranged attack with the weapon or piece of ammunition you just caught, as part of the same reaction. You make this attack with proficiency, regardless of your weapon proficiencies, and the missile counts as a monk weapon for the attack, which has a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet.
features.summary: Reaction when hit by a ranged weapon attack: reduce damage by 1d10 + Dex modifier + monk level. If reduced to 0 and you have a free hand, catch it and may spend 1 ki to throw it back as a monk-weapon attack with proficiency.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
features.summary: At 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th and 19th level: +2 to one ability score or +1 to two, to a maximum of 20.

features.name: Slow Fall
features.desc: Beginning at 4th level, you can use your reaction when you fall to reduce any falling damage you take by an amount equal to five times your monk level.
features.summary: Reaction while falling: reduce fall damage by 5 x monk level.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.desc: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
features.summary: Attack twice when you take the Attack action.

features.name: Stunning Strike
features.desc: Starting at 5th level, you can interfere with the flow of ki in an opponent's body. When you hit another creature with a melee weapon attack, you can spend 1 ki point to attempt a stunning strike. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be stunned until the end of your next turn.
features.summary: On a melee weapon hit, spend 1 ki: target makes a Con save or is stunned until the end of your next turn.

features.name: Ki-Empowered Strikes
features.desc: Starting at 6th level, your unarmed strikes count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.
features.summary: Unarmed strikes count as magical for overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical damage.

features.name: Evasion
features.desc: At 7th level, your instinctive agility lets you dodge out of the way of certain area effects, such as a blue dragon's lightning breath or a fireball spell. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.
features.summary: On a Dex save for half damage: no damage on a success, half on a failure.

features.name: Stillness of Mind
features.desc: Starting at 7th level, you can use your action to end one effect on yourself that is causing you to be charmed or frightened.
features.summary: Use your action to end one charmed or frightened effect on yourself.

features.name: Purity of Body
features.desc: At 10th level, your mastery of the ki flowing through you makes you immune to disease and poison.
features.summary: Immune to disease and poison.

features.name: Tongue of the Sun and Moon
features.desc: Starting at 13th level, you learn to touch the ki of other minds so that you understand all spoken languages. Moreover, any creature that can understand a language can understand what you say.
features.summary: Understand all spoken languages, and any creature that knows a language understands your speech.

features.name: Diamond Soul
features.desc:
Beginning at 14th level, your mastery of ki grants you proficiency in all saving throws.
Additionally, whenever you make a saving throw and fail, you can spend 1 ki point to reroll it and take the second result.
features.summary: Proficiency in all saving throws; spend 1 ki to reroll a failed save and use the new result.

features.name: Timeless Body
features.desc: At 15th level, your ki sustains you so that you suffer none of the frailty of old age, and you can't be aged magically. You can still die of old age, however. In addition, you no longer need food or water.
features.summary: No frailty from old age, immune to magical aging, and no longer need food or water (can still die of old age).

features.name: Empty Body
features.desc:
Beginning at 18th level, you can use your action to spend 4 ki points to become invisible for 1 minute. During that time, you also have resistance to all damage but force damage.
Additionally, you can spend 8 ki points to cast the astral projection spell, without needing material components. When you do so, you can't take any other creatures with you.
features.summary: Action + 4 ki: invisible for 1 minute with resistance to all damage except force. 8 ki: cast astral projection without material components, on yourself only.

features.name: Perfect Self
features.desc: At 20th level, when you roll for initiative and have no ki points remaining, you regain 4 ki points.
features.summary: When you roll initiative with 0 ki remaining, regain 4 ki.

features.name: Open Hand Technique
features.desc:
Starting when you choose this tradition at 3rd level, you can manipulate your enemy's ki when you harness your own. Whenever you hit a creature with one of the attacks granted by your Flurry of Blows, you can impose one of the following effects on that target:
- It must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be knocked prone.
- It must make a Strength saving throw. If it fails, you can push it up to 15 feet away from you.
- It can't take reactions until the end of your next turn.
features.summary: Flurry of Blows hits can impose one effect: Dex save or prone, Str save or pushed up to 15 ft, or no reactions until the end of your next turn.

features.name: Wholeness of Body
features.desc: At 6th level, you gain the ability to heal yourself. As an action, you can regain hit points equal to three times your monk level. You must finish a long rest before you can use this feature again.
features.summary: Action: regain hit points equal to 3 x monk level. Once per long rest.

features.name: Tranquility
features.desc: Beginning at 11th level, you can enter a special meditation that surrounds you with an aura of peace. At the end of a long rest, you gain the effect of a sanctuary spell that lasts until the start of your next long rest (the spell can end early as normal). The saving throw DC for the spell equals 8 + your Wisdom modifier + your proficiency bonus.
features.summary: At the end of each long rest, gain a sanctuary effect lasting until your next long rest (save DC 8 + Wis + prof); ends early as the spell does.

features.name: Quivering Palm
features.desc:
At 17th level, you gain the ability to set up lethal vibrations in someone's body. When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you can spend 3 ki points to start these imperceptible vibrations, which last for a number of days equal to your monk level. The vibrations are harmless unless you use your action to end them. To do so, you and the target must be on the same plane of existence. When you use this action, the creature must make a Constitution saving throw. If it fails, it is reduced to 0 hit points. If it succeeds, it takes 10d10 necrotic damage.
You can have only one creature under the effect of this feature at a time. You can choose to end the vibrations harmlessly without using an action.
features.summary: On an unarmed hit, spend 3 ki to plant vibrations lasting monk-level days; later use an action (same plane) to force a Con save: fail drops it to 0 HP, success deals 10d10 necrotic. One target at a time.

features.name: Shadow Arts
features.summary: Action + 2 ki: cast darkness, darkvision, pass without trace or silence with no material components. Also learn the minor illusion cantrip if you lack it.

features.name: Shadow Step
features.summary: In dim light or darkness, bonus action to teleport up to 60 ft to another dim or dark space you can see; advantage on your first melee attack before the end of the turn.

features.name: Cloak of Shadows
features.summary: In dim light or darkness, use your action to become invisible until you attack, cast a spell, or enter bright light.

features.name: Opportunist
features.summary: Reaction when a creature within 5 ft is hit by someone else's attack: make a melee attack against it.

features.name: Disciple of the Elements
features.summary: Know Elemental Attunement plus one other elemental discipline; learn one more at 6th, 11th and 17th level (may swap one each time). Discipline spells need no material components; from 5th level extra ki upcasts them, capped by the Spells and Ki Points table (3 ki at 5th-8th, 4 at 9th-12th, 5 at 13th-16th, 6 at 17th-20th).

choices.name: Breath of Winter
choices.summary: 6 ki: cast cone of cold.

choices.name: Clench of the North Wind
choices.summary: 3 ki: cast hold person.

choices.name: Elemental Attunement
choices.summary: Action: minor elemental tricks - harmless sensory effect, light/snuff a small flame, chill or warm up to 1 lb for 1 hour, or shape a 1-foot cube of earth, fire, water or mist for 1 minute.

choices.name: Eternal Mountain Defense
choices.summary: 5 ki: cast stoneskin on yourself.

choices.name: Fangs of the Fire Snake
choices.summary: 1 ki when taking the Attack action: unarmed reach +10 ft for the turn and those hits deal fire damage; +1 ki on a hit for an extra 1d10 fire.
choices.prerequisite: 1 ki (+1 ki per hit for extra damage)

choices.name: Fist of Four Thunders
choices.summary: 2 ki: cast thunderwave.

choices.name: Fist of Unbroken Air
choices.summary: Action + 2 ki: creature within 30 ft makes a Str save or takes 3d10 bludgeoning (+1d10 per extra ki), is pushed up to 20 ft and knocked prone; half damage only on a success.

choices.name: Flames of the Phoenix
choices.summary: 4 ki: cast fireball.

choices.name: Gong of the Summit
choices.summary: 3 ki: cast shatter.

choices.name: Mist Stance
choices.summary: 4 ki: cast gaseous form on yourself.

choices.name: Ride the Wind
choices.summary: 4 ki: cast fly on yourself.

choices.name: River of Hungry Flame
choices.summary: 5 ki: cast wall of fire.

choices.name: Rush of the Gale Spirits
choices.summary: 2 ki: cast gust of wind.

choices.name: Shape the Flowing River
choices.summary: Action + 1 ki: reshape ice or water in a cube up to 30 ft on a side within 120 ft - freeze/thaw, raise or lower elevation, dig trenches, raise walls or pillars (changes up to half the largest dimension; can't trap or harm creatures).

choices.name: Sweeping Cinder Strike
choices.summary: 2 ki: cast burning hands.

choices.name: Water Whip
choices.summary: Bonus action + 2 ki: creature within 30 ft makes a Dex save or takes 3d10 bludgeoning (+1d10 per extra ki) and is knocked prone or pulled up to 25 ft closer; half damage only on a success.

choices.name: Wave of Rolling Earth
choices.summary: 6 ki: cast wall of stone.

startingEquipmentOptions.desc: (a) a shortsword or (b) any simple weapon
(a) a dungeoneer’s pack or (b) an explorer’s pack

features.name: Divine Sense
features.desc:
The presence of strong evil registers on your senses like a noxious odor, and powerful good rings like heavenly music in your ears. As an action, you can open your awareness to detect such forces. Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of any celestial, fiend, or undead within 60 feet of you that is not behind total cover. You know the type (celestial, fiend, or undead) of any being whose presence you sense, but not its identity. Within the same radius, you also detect the presence of any place or object that has been consecrated or desecrated, as with the hallow spell.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to 1 + your Charisma modifier. When you finish a long rest, you regain all expended uses.
features.summary: Action: until the end of your next turn, learn the location and type (celestial, fiend, undead) of such creatures within 60 ft. not behind total cover, plus consecrated/desecrated places or objects.

features.name: Lay on Hands
features.desc:
Your blessed touch can heal wounds. You have a pool of healing power that replenishes when you take a long rest. With that pool, you can restore a total number of hit points equal to your paladin level x 5.
As an action, you can touch a creature and draw power from the pool to restore a number of hit points to that creature, up to the maximum amount remaining in your pool.
Alternatively, you can expend 5 hit points from your pool of healing to cure the target of one disease or neutralize one poison affecting it. You can cure multiple diseases and neutralize multiple poisons with a single use of Lay on Hands, expending hit points separately for each one.
This feature has no effect on undead and constructs.
features.summary: Healing pool of 5 x paladin level HP. Action, touch: restore any amount of HP from the pool, or spend 5 points per disease cured / poison neutralized. No effect on undead or constructs.

features.name: Fighting Style
features.desc: At 2nd level, you adopt a style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.
features.summary: Pick one fighting style from the paladin list (Defense, Dueling, Great Weapon Fighting, Protection). The same style can never be taken twice.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.desc: By 2nd level, you have learned to draw on divine magic through meditation and prayer to cast spells as a cleric does.
features.summary: Half-caster using Charisma. Prepare CHA mod + half paladin level (round down, min 1) spells from the paladin list after a long rest; slots per the class table. Holy symbol can be a focus.

features.name: Divine Smite
features.desc: Starting at 2nd level, when you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can expend one spell slot to deal radiant damage to the target, in addition to the weapon's damage. The extra damage is 2d8 for a 1st-level spell slot, plus 1d8 for each spell level higher than 1st, to a maximum of 5d8. The damage increases by 1d8 if the target is an undead or a fiend.
features.summary: On a melee weapon hit, spend a paladin spell slot for extra radiant damage: 2d8 for 1st level, +1d8 per slot level above 1st (max 5d8), +1d8 more vs. undead or fiends.

features.name: Divine Health
features.desc: By 3rd level, the divine magic flowing through you makes you immune to disease.
features.summary: You are immune to disease.

features.name: Sacred Oath
features.desc:
When you reach 3rd level, you swear the oath that binds you as a paladin forever. Up to this time you have been in a preparatory stage, committed to the path but not yet sworn to it. Now you choose an oath, such as the Oath of Devotion.
Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 15th, and 20th level. Those features include oath spells and the Channel Divinity feature.
features.summary: Swear an oath (Devotion, Ancients, or Vengeance). It grants features at 3rd, 7th, 15th, and 20th level, including oath spells and Channel Divinity options.

features.name: Oath Spells
features.desc:
Each oath has a list of associated spells. You gain access to these spells at the levels specified in the oath description. Once you gain access to an oath spell, you always have it prepared. Oath spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day.
If you gain an oath spell that doesn't appear on the paladin spell list, the spell is nonetheless a paladin spell for you.
features.summary: Part of Sacred Oath. Each oath lists spells gained at paladin levels 3/5/9/13/17; they are always prepared, don't count against your prepared total, and count as paladin spells.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.desc:
Your oath allows you to channel divine energy to fuel magical effects. Each Channel Divinity option provided by your oath explains how to use it.
When you use your Channel Divinity, you choose which option to use. You must then finish a short or long rest to use your Channel Divinity again.
Some Channel Divinity effects require saving throws. When you use such an effect from this class, the DC equals your paladin spell save DC.
features.summary: Part of Sacred Oath. Use one Channel Divinity option granted by your oath; then you must finish a short or long rest before using it again. Save DC = your paladin spell save DC.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
features.summary: At 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th and 19th level: +2 to one ability score or +1 to two, max 20.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.desc: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
features.summary: When you take the Attack action, you make two attacks instead of one.

features.name: Aura of Protection
features.desc:
Starting at 6th level, whenever you or a friendly creature within 10 feet of you must make a saving throw, the creature gains a bonus to the saving throw equal to your Charisma modifier (with a minimum bonus of +1). You must be conscious to grant this bonus.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.
features.summary: While you are conscious, you and friendly creatures within 10 ft. add your Charisma modifier (minimum +1) to all saving throws. Range becomes 30 ft. at 18th level.

features.name: Aura of Courage
features.desc:
Starting at 10th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you can't be frightened while you are conscious.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.
features.summary: While you are conscious, you and friendly creatures within 10 ft. can't be frightened. Range becomes 30 ft. at 18th level.

features.name: Improved Divine Smite
features.desc: By 11th level, you are so suffused with righteous might that all your melee weapon strikes carry divine power with them. Whenever you hit a creature with a melee weapon, the creature takes an extra 1d8 radiant damage. If you also use your Divine Smite with an attack, you add this damage to the extra damage of your Divine Smite.
features.summary: Every melee weapon hit deals an extra 1d8 radiant damage; this stacks with Divine Smite.

features.name: Cleansing Touch
features.desc:
Beginning at 14th level, you can use your action to end one spell on yourself or on one willing creature that you touch.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once). You regain expended uses when you finish a long rest.
features.summary: Action: end one spell on yourself or on a willing creature you touch.

features.name: Aura improvements
features.desc: At 18th level, the range of your auras increase to 30 feet.
features.summary: Your paladin auras (Aura of Protection, Aura of Courage, and your oath's 7th-level aura) extend from 10 ft. to 30 ft.

features.name: Oath Spells
features.summary: Always-prepared Oath of Devotion spells (see spells).

features.name: Sacred Weapon
features.summary: Channel Divinity, action: for 1 minute a held weapon adds your CHA mod (min +1) to attack rolls, sheds bright light 20 ft. (dim 20 ft. more), and counts as magical. Ends if dropped or you fall unconscious.

features.name: Turn the Unholy
features.summary: Channel Divinity, action: each fiend or undead within 30 ft. that can see or hear you makes a WIS save or is turned for 1 minute or until damaged (must flee, no reactions, only Dash/escape/Dodge).

features.name: Aura of Devotion
features.desc:
Starting at 7th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you can't be charmed while you are conscious.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.
features.summary: While you are conscious, you and friendly creatures within 10 ft. can't be charmed. Range becomes 30 ft. at 18th level.

features.name: Purity of Spirit
features.desc: Beginning at 15th level, you are always under the effects of a protection from evil and good spell.
features.summary: You are permanently under the effect of protection from evil and good.

features.name: Holy Nimbus
features.desc:
At 20th level, as an action, you can emanate an aura of sunlight. For 1 minute, bright light shines from you in a 30-foot radius, and dim light shines 30 feet beyond that.
Whenever an enemy creature starts its turn in the bright light, the creature takes 10 radiant damage.
In addition, for the duration, you have advantage on saving throws against spells cast by fiends or undead.
features.summary: Action: for 1 minute emit bright sunlight 30 ft. (dim 30 ft. more); enemies starting their turn in the bright light take 10 radiant damage; you have advantage on saves vs. spells cast by fiends or undead.

choices.name: Sacred Weapon
choices.summary: Empower a held weapon: +CHA to attacks, light, magical, 1 minute.

choices.name: Turn the Unholy
choices.summary: Turn fiends and undead within 30 ft. on a failed WIS save.

features.name: Oath Spells
features.summary: Always-prepared Oath of the Ancients spells (see spells).

features.name: Nature's Wrath
features.summary: Channel Divinity, action: spectral vines attack a creature within 10 ft. that you can see; it makes a STR or DEX save (its choice) or is restrained, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns.

features.name: Turn the Faithless
features.summary: Channel Divinity, action: each fey or fiend within 30 ft. that can hear you makes a WIS save or is turned for 1 minute or until damaged; a turned creature's disguised true form is revealed.

features.name: Aura of Warding
features.summary: You and friendly creatures within 10 ft. have resistance to damage from spells. Range becomes 30 ft. at 18th level.

features.name: Undying Sentinel
features.summary: When reduced to 0 HP but not killed outright, you can drop to 1 HP instead. You also suffer no drawbacks of old age and can't be magically aged.

features.name: Elder Champion
features.summary: Action: transform for 1 minute. Regain 10 HP at the start of each of your turns, cast 1-action paladin spells as a bonus action, and enemies within 10 ft. have disadvantage on saves vs. your paladin spells and Channel Divinity.

choices.name: Nature's Wrath
choices.summary: Restrain one creature within 10 ft. with spectral vines (STR or DEX save).

choices.name: Turn the Faithless
choices.summary: Turn fey and fiends within 30 ft. on a failed WIS save.

features.name: Oath Spells
features.summary: Always-prepared Oath of Vengeance spells (see spells).

features.name: Abjure Enemy
features.summary: Channel Divinity, action: one creature within 60 ft. you can see makes a WIS save (fiends/undead at disadvantage; frighten-immune creatures unaffected). Fail: frightened 1 minute or until damaged, speed 0. Success: speed halved 1 minute or until damaged.

features.name: Vow of Enmity
features.summary: Channel Divinity, bonus action: choose a creature within 10 ft. you can see; you have advantage on attack rolls against it for 1 minute or until it drops to 0 HP or falls unconscious.

features.name: Relentless Avenger
features.summary: When you hit with an opportunity attack, you may move up to half your speed as part of that reaction, without provoking opportunity attacks.

features.name: Soul of Vengeance
features.summary: When the target of your Vow of Enmity makes an attack, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against it if it is in range.

features.name: Avenging Angel
features.summary: Action: transform for 1 hour. Gain a 60 ft. flying speed and a 30 ft. aura; enemies entering or starting a turn there for the first time make a WIS save or are frightened 1 minute or until damaged, and attacks against them have advantage.

choices.name: Abjure Enemy
choices.summary: Frighten and root one creature within 60 ft. (WIS save).

choices.name: Vow of Enmity
choices.summary: Advantage on attacks vs. one creature within 10 ft. for 1 minute.

choices.name: Defense
choices.summary: +1 AC while you wear armor.

choices.name: Dueling
choices.summary: +2 damage with a melee weapon held in one hand when you hold no other weapon.

choices.name: Great Weapon Fighting
choices.summary: Reroll 1s and 2s on damage dice for two-handed melee weapon attacks (weapon must be two-handed or versatile); must keep the new roll.

choices.name: Protection
choices.summary: Reaction: impose disadvantage on an attack against a creature (not you) within 5 ft. of you that you can see. Requires a shield.

features.name: Favored Enemy
features.desc:
Beginning at 1st level, you have significant experience studying, tracking, hunting, and even talking to a certain type of enemy.
Choose a type of favored enemy: aberrations, beasts, celestials, constructs, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, giants, monstrosities, oozes, plants, or undead. Alternatively, you can select two races of humanoid (such as gnolls and orcs) as favored enemies.
You have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track your favored enemies, as well as on Intelligence checks to recall information about them.
When you gain this feature, you also learn one language of your choice that is spoken by your favored enemies, if they speak one at all.
You choose one additional favored enemy, as well as an associated language, at 6th and 14th level. As you gain levels, your choices should reflect the types of monsters you have encountered on your adventures.
features.summary: Pick a creature type (or two humanoid races). Advantage on WIS (Survival) to track them and INT checks to recall lore about them; learn one of their languages. Extra choice (and language) at 6th and 14th level.

features.name: Natural Explorer
features.desc:
You are particularly familiar with one type of natural environment and are adept at traveling and surviving in such regions. Choose one type of favored terrain: arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, or swamp. When you make an Intelligence or Wisdom check related to your favored terrain, your proficiency bonus is doubled if you are using a skill that you're proficient in.
While traveling for an hour or more in your favored terrain, you gain the following benefits:
- Difficult terrain doesn't slow your group's travel.
- Your group can't become lost except by magical means.
- Even when you are engaged in another activity while traveling (such as foraging, navigating, or tracking), you remain alert to danger.
- If you are traveling alone, you can move stealthily at a normal pace.
- When you forage, you find twice as much food as you normally would.
- While tracking other creatures, you also learn their exact number, their sizes, and how long ago they passed through the area.
You choose additional favored terrain types at 6th and 10th level.
features.summary: Pick a favored terrain: double proficiency on proficient INT/WIS checks about it, and travel perks there (no slowdown from difficult terrain, can't get lost, double forage, etc.). Extra terrain at 6th and 10th level.

features.name: Fighting Style
features.desc: At 2nd level, you adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.
features.summary: Pick one fighting style from the ranger list (Archery, Defense, Dueling, Two-Weapon Fighting). The same style can never be taken twice.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.desc: By the time you reach 2nd level, you have learned to use the magical essence of nature to cast spells, much as a druid does.
features.summary: Half-caster using Wisdom with a fixed number of known spells (Spells Known column); can swap one known spell on each ranger level-up. Slots per the class table, regained on a long rest.

features.name: Ranger Archetype
features.desc: At 3rd level, you choose an archetype that you strive to emulate, such as the Hunter. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 11th, and 15th level.
features.summary: Choose Hunter or Beast Master; the archetype grants features at 3rd, 7th, 11th and 15th level.

features.name: Primeval Awareness
features.desc: Beginning at 3rd level, you can use your action and expend one ranger spell slot to focus your awareness on the region around you. For 1 minute per level of the spell slot you expend, you can sense whether the following types of creatures are present within 1 mile of you (or within up to 6 miles if you are in your favored terrain): aberrations, celestials, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, and undead. This feature doesn't reveal the creatures' location or number.
features.summary: Action + one ranger spell slot: for 1 minute per slot level, sense whether aberrations, celestials, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends or undead are within 1 mile (6 miles in favored terrain); no location or count.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
features.summary: At 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th and 19th level: +2 to one ability score or +1 to two, max 20.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.desc: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
features.summary: When you take the Attack action, you make two attacks instead of one.

features.name: Land's Stride
features.desc:
Starting at 8th level, moving through nonmagical difficult terrain costs you no extra movement. You can also pass through nonmagical plants without being slowed by them and without taking damage from them if they have thorns, spines, or a similar hazard.
In addition, you have advantage on saving throws against plants that are magically created or manipulated to impede movement, such those created by the entangle spell.
features.summary: Nonmagical difficult terrain costs no extra movement; pass through nonmagical plants unhindered and unharmed by thorns; advantage on saves vs. magical plants that impede movement (e.g. entangle).

features.name: Hide in Plain Sight
features.desc:
Starting at 10th level, you can spend 1 minute creating camouflage for yourself. You must have access to fresh mud, dirt, plants, soot, and other naturally occurring materials with which to create your camouflage.
Once you are camouflaged in this way, you can try to hide by pressing yourself up against a solid surface, such as a tree or wall, that is at least as tall and wide as you are. You gain a +10 bonus to Dexterity (Stealth) checks as long as you remain there without moving or taking actions. Once you move or take an action or a reaction, you must camouflage yourself again to gain this benefit.
features.summary: Spend 1 minute camouflaging with natural materials; while pressed against a solid surface at least your size and not moving or acting, gain +10 to DEX (Stealth). Moving or acting ends it.

features.name: Vanish
features.desc: Starting at 14th level, you can use the Hide action as a bonus action on your turn. Also, you can't be tracked by nonmagical means, unless you choose to leave a trail.
features.summary: Take the Hide action as a bonus action; you can't be tracked by nonmagical means unless you choose to leave a trail.

features.name: Feral Senses
features.desc:
At 18th level, you gain preternatural senses that help you fight creatures you can't see. When you attack a creature you can't see, your inability to see it doesn't impose disadvantage on your attack rolls against it.
You are also aware of the location of any invisible creature within 30 feet of you, provided that the creature isn't hidden from you and you aren't blinded or deafened.
features.summary: Not seeing a creature doesn't give you disadvantage on attacks against it; you know where invisible creatures within 30 ft. are if they aren't hidden and you aren't blinded or deafened.

features.name: Foe Slayer
features.desc: At 20th level, you become an unparalleled hunter of your enemies. Once on each of your turns, you can add your Wisdom modifier to the attack roll or the damage roll of an attack you make against one of your favored enemies. You can choose to use this feature before or after the roll, but before any effects of the roll are applied.
features.summary: Once per turn, add your WIS modifier to the attack roll or damage roll of an attack against a favored enemy, choosing before or after the roll but before effects apply.

features.name: Hunter's Prey
features.desc:
At 3rd level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Colossus Slayer
Giant Killer
Horde Breaker
features.summary: Choose one: Colossus Slayer, Giant Killer, or Horde Breaker.

features.name: Defensive Tactics
features.desc:
At 7th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Escape the Horde
Multiattack Defense
Steel Will
features.summary: Choose one: Escape the Horde, Multiattack Defense, or Steel Will.

features.name: Multiattack

choices.name: Giant Killer

choices.name: Horde Breaker

choices.name: Escape the Horde

choices.name: Multiattack Defense

choices.name: Stand Against the Tide

choices.name: Uncanny Dodge

features.name: Ranger's Companion

Add proficiency bonus to its AC, attacks, damage, and proficient saves/skills; HP max is the greater of normal or 4 x ranger level. It acts on your initiative only when commanded: your action orders Attack, Dash, Disengage, Dodge or Help. Replace it with 8 hours of bonding.

features.name: Exceptional Training
features.summary: On a turn your companion doesn't attack, a bonus action can command it to Dash, Disengage, Dodge, or Help.

features.name: Bestial Fury
features.summary: Your companion makes two attacks when commanded to take the Attack action.

features.name: Share Spells
features.summary: A spell you cast targeting yourself can also affect your companion if it is within 30 ft.

features.name: Expertise
features.desc:
At 1st level, choose two of your skill proficiencies, or one of your skill proficiencies and your proficiency with thieves' tools. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies.
At 6th level, you can choose two more of your proficiencies (in skills or with thieves' tools) to gain this benefit
features.summary: Pick two skill proficiencies (or one skill plus thieves' tools); your proficiency bonus is doubled for checks using them. Pick two more at 6th level.

features.name: Sneak Attack
features.desc:
Beginning at 1st level, you know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack if you have advantage on the attack roll. The attack must use a finesse or a ranged weapon.
You don't need advantage on the attack roll if another enemy of the target is within 5 feet of it, that enemy isn't incapacitated, and you don't have disadvantage on the attack roll.
The amount of the extra damage increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Rogue table.
features.summary: Once per turn, add the Sneak Attack dice to one finesse or ranged weapon hit if you have advantage, or if an active ally is within 5 ft. of the target and you lack disadvantage.

features.name: Thieves' Cant
features.desc:
During your rogue training you learned thieves' cant, a secret mix of dialect, jargon, and code that allows you to hide messages in seemingly normal conversation. Only another creature that knows thieves' cant understands such messages. It takes four times longer to convey such a message than it does to speak the same idea plainly.
In addition, you understand a set of secret signs and symbols used to convey short, simple messages, such as whether an area is dangerous or the territory of a thieves' guild, whether loot is nearby, or whether the people in an area are easy marks or will provide a safe house for thieves on the run.
features.summary: You know the secret rogue jargon for hiding messages in ordinary talk (takes four times as long) plus a set of signs and symbols for short coded messages.

features.name: Cunning Action
features.desc: Starting at 2nd level, your quick thinking and agility allow you to move and act quickly. You can take a bonus action on each of your turns in combat. This action can be used only to take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action.
features.summary: Each turn in combat you may take a bonus action to Dash, Disengage, or Hide.

features.name: Roguish Archetype
features.desc: At 3rd level, you choose an archetype that you emulate in the exercise of your rogue abilities, such as Thief. Additional archetypes are available in the original source material. Your archetype choice grants you features at 3rd level and then again at 9th, 13th, and 17th level.
features.summary: Choose Thief, Assassin, or Arcane Trickster; it grants features at 3rd, 9th, 13th, and 17th level.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 10th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
features.summary: At 4th, 8th, 10th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, raise one ability score by 2 or two scores by 1 (maximum 20).

features.name: Uncanny Dodge
features.desc: Starting at 5th level, when an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the attack's damage against you.
features.summary: Reaction: when an attacker you can see hits you, halve that attack's damage.

features.name: Evasion
features.desc: Beginning at 7th level, you can nimbly dodge out of the way of certain area effects, such as a red dragon's fiery breath or an ice storm spell. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.
features.summary: On a Dexterity save against an effect that deals half damage on success, you take none on a success and half on a failure.

features.name: Reliable Talent
features.desc: By 11th level, you have refined your chosen skills until they approach perfection. Whenever you make an ability check that lets you add your proficiency bonus, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.
features.summary: On any ability check that adds your proficiency bonus, a d20 roll of 9 or lower counts as 10.

features.name: Blindsense
features.desc: Starting at 14th level, if you are able to hear, you are aware of the location of any hidden or invisible creature within 10 feet of you.
features.summary: While you can hear, you know where any hidden or invisible creature within 10 ft. of you is.

features.name: Slippery Mind
features.desc: By 15th level, you have acquired greater mental strength. You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws.
features.summary: You become proficient in Wisdom saving throws.

features.name: Elusive
features.desc: Beginning at 18th level, you are so evasive that attackers rarely gain the upper hand against you. No attack roll has advantage against you while you aren't incapacitated.
features.summary: Unless you are incapacitated, attack rolls against you can never have advantage.

features.name: Stroke of Luck
features.desc:
At 20th level, you have an uncanny knack for succeeding when you need to. If your attack misses a target within range, you can turn the miss into a hit. Alternatively, if you fail an ability check, you can treat the d20 roll as a 20.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
features.summary: Turn a missed attack against a target in range into a hit, or treat a failed ability check's d20 as a 20. Once per short or long rest.

features.name: Fast Hands
features.desc: Starting at 3rd level, you can use the bonus action granted by your Cunning Action to make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, use your thieves' tools to disarm a trap or open a lock, or take the Use an Object action.
features.summary: Cunning Action's bonus action can also be a Sleight of Hand check, using thieves' tools on a trap or lock, or the Use an Object action.

features.name: Second-Story Work
features.desc:
When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain the ability to climb faster than normal; climbing no longer costs you extra movement.
In addition, when you make a running jump, the distance you cover increases by a number of feet equal to your Dexterity modifier.
features.summary: Climbing costs no extra movement, and running jumps go farther by a number of feet equal to your Dexterity modifier.

features.name: Supreme Sneak
features.desc: Starting at 9th level, you have advantage on a Dexterity (Stealth) check if you move no more than half your speed on the same turn.
features.summary: Advantage on Stealth checks on a turn in which you move no more than half your speed.

features.name: Use Magic Device
features.desc: By 13th level, you have learned enough about the workings of magic that you can improvise the use of items even when they are not intended for you. You ignore all class, race, and level requirements on the use of magic items.
features.summary: You disregard class, race, and level requirements when using magic items.

features.name: Thief's Reflexes
features.desc: When you reach 17th level, you have become adept at laying ambushes and quickly escaping danger. You can take two turns during the first round of any combat. You take your first turn at your normal initiative and your second turn at your initiative minus 10. You can't use this feature when you are surprised.
features.summary: In the first round of combat you take two turns: one at your initiative and a second at initiative minus 10. Not usable when surprised.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.summary: Gain proficiency with the disguise kit and the poisoner's kit.

features.name: Assassinate
features.summary: Advantage on attacks against creatures that have not yet acted in the combat; any hit against a surprised creature is a critical hit.

features.name: Infiltration Expertise
features.summary: Spend 7 days and 25 gp to build a reliable false identity (not someone else's); while you use it, others accept it unless given clear reason to doubt.

features.name: Impostor
features.summary: After 3 hours studying a person's speech, writing, and behaviour you can mimic them; casual observers are fooled and you get advantage on Deception checks to avoid detection.

features.name: Death Strike
features.summary: When you hit a surprised creature, it makes a Con save (DC 8 + Dex mod + prof); on a failure the attack's damage is doubled.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.summary: Int-based wizard spellcasting per the Arcane Trickster table: mage hand plus two other cantrips; leveled spells mostly enchantment or illusion, except those learned at 3rd, 8th, 14th, and 20th level, which may be any school.

features.name: Mage Hand Legerdemain
features.summary: Your mage hand can be invisible and can stow or retrieve items in containers others wear and use thieves' tools at range (Sleight of Hand vs. Perception to go unnoticed); control it with Cunning Action.

features.name: Magical Ambush
features.summary: If you are hidden when you cast a spell on a creature, it has disadvantage on saves against that spell this turn.

features.name: Versatile Trickster
features.summary: Bonus action: target a creature within 5 ft. of your mage hand to gain advantage on attacks against it until the end of the turn.

features.name: Spell Thief
features.summary: Reaction when a spell targets or includes you: caster saves with its spellcasting modifier vs. your DC; on a failure you negate it for you and, if it is 1st level or higher and castable by you, you know it for 8 hours while the caster cannot cast it.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.desc: An event in your past, or in the life of a parent or ancestor, left an indelible mark on you, infusing you with arcane magic. This font of magic, whatever its origin, fuels your spells.
features.summary: Charisma-based casting from the sorcerer list; cantrips, spells known, and slots per the Sorcerer table. Swap one known spell on level-up. Arcane focus usable.

features.name: Sorcerous Origin
features.desc:
Choose a sorcerous origin, which describes the source of your innate magical power, such as Draconic Bloodline.
Your choice grants you features when you choose it at 1st level and again at 6th, 14th, and 18th level.
features.summary: Choose Draconic Bloodline or Wild Magic; it grants features at 1st, 6th, 14th, and 18th level.

features.name: Font of Magic
features.desc:
At 2nd level, you tap into a deep wellspring of magic within yourself. This wellspring is represented by sorcery points, which allow you to create a variety of magical effects.
Sorcery Points
You have 2 sorcery points, and you gain more as you reach higher levels, as shown in the Sorcery Points column of the Sorcerer table. You can never have more sorcery points than shown on the table for your level. You regain all spent sorcery points when you finish a long rest.
features.summary: Gain sorcery points (table column, regained on a long rest). Flexible Casting: bonus action to turn points into a slot of up to 5th level, or a slot into points equal to its level.

features.name: Metamagic
features.desc:
At 3rd level, you gain the ability to twist your spells to suit your needs. You gain two of the following Metamagic options of your choice. You gain another one at 10th and 17th level.
You can use only one Metamagic option on a spell when you cast it, unless otherwise noted.
features.summary: Learn two Metamagic options, plus one more at 10th and 17th level. Normally only one option can be applied per spell.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
features.summary: At 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, raise one ability score by 2 or two scores by 1 (maximum 20).

features.name: Sorcerous Restoration
features.desc: At 20th level, you regain 4 expended sorcery points whenever you finish a short rest.
features.summary: Regain 4 spent sorcery points whenever you finish a short rest.

features.name: Dragon Ancestor
features.desc:
At 1st level, you choose one type of dragon as your ancestor. The damage type associated with each dragon is used by features you gain later.
You can speak, read, and write Draconic. Additionally, whenever you make a Charisma check when interacting with dragons, your proficiency bonus is doubled if it applies to the check.
features.summary: Choose a dragon type (sets your ancestry damage type). You know Draconic, and double your proficiency bonus on Charisma checks with dragons when it applies.

features.name: Draconic Resilience
features.desc:
As magic flows through your body, it causes physical traits of your dragon ancestors to emerge. At 1st level, your hit point maximum increases by 1 and increases by 1 again whenever you gain a level in this class.
Additionally, parts of your skin are covered by a thin sheen of dragon-like scales. When you aren't wearing armor, your AC equals 13 + your Dexterity modifier.
features.summary: +1 hit point maximum per sorcerer level; unarmored AC is 13 + Dex modifier.

features.name: Elemental Affinity
features.desc: Starting at 6th level, when you cast a spell that deals damage of the type associated with your draconic ancestry, you can add your Charisma modifier to one damage roll of that spell. At the same time, you can spend 1 sorcery point to gain resistance to that damage type for 1 hour.
features.summary: Add Cha modifier to damage from spells of your ancestry type; spend 1 sorcery point to resist that type for 1 hour.

features.name: Dragon Wings
features.desc:
At 14th level, you gain the ability to sprout a pair of dragon wings from your back, gaining a flying speed equal to your current speed. You can create these wings as a bonus action on your turn. They last until you dismiss them as a bonus action on your turn.
You can't manifest your wings while wearing armor unless the armor is made to accommodate them, and clothing not made to accommodate your wings might be destroyed when you manifest them.
features.summary: Bonus action to grow or dismiss wings giving a fly speed equal to your speed; not while wearing armor not made for them.

features.name: Draconic Presence
features.desc: Beginning at 18th level, you can channel the dread presence of your dragon ancestor, causing those around you to become awestruck or frightened. As an action, you can spend 5 sorcery points to draw on this power and exude an aura of awe or fear (your choice) to a distance of 60 feet. For 1 minute or until you lose your concentration (as if you were casting a concentration spell), each hostile creature that starts its turn in this aura must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed (if you chose awe) or frightened (if you chose fear) until the aura ends. A creature that succeeds on this saving throw is immune to your aura for 24 hours.
features.summary: Action, 5 sorcery points: 60-ft. aura (concentration, up to 1 minute); hostiles starting their turn in it make a Wis save or are charmed (awe) or frightened (fear); success grants 24-hour immunity.

features.name: Otherworldly Patron
features.desc: At 1st level, you have struck a bargain with an otherworldly being of your choice, such as the Fiend. Your choice grants you features at 1st level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.
features.summary: Choose a patron (Archfey, Fiend, or Great Old One); it grants features at 1st, 6th, 10th, and 14th level and an expanded spell list.

features.name: Pact Magic
features.desc: Your arcane research and the magic bestowed on you by your patron have given you facility with spells.
features.summary: Charisma-based casting from the warlock list. Few slots, all cast at the table's Slot Level; every slot returns on a short or long rest. Spells known can be swapped on level-up; arcane focus allowed.

features.name: Eldritch Invocations
features.desc:
In your study of occult lore, you have unearthed eldritch invocations, fragments of forbidden knowledge that imbue you with an abiding magical ability.
At 2nd level, you gain two eldritch invocations of your choice. Your invocation options are detailed at the end of the class description. When you gain certain warlock levels, you gain additional invocations of your choice, as shown in the Invocations Known column of the Warlock table.
Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the invocations you know and replace it with another invocation that you could learn at that level.
features.summary: Learn two invocations at 2nd level, more per the Invocations Known column; on each warlock level-up one known invocation may be replaced with another you qualify for.

features.name: Pact Boon
features.desc: At 3rd level, your otherworldly patron bestows a gift upon you for your loyal service. You gain one of the following features of your choice.
features.summary: Your patron grants one boon of your choice: Pact of the Chain, Pact of the Blade, or Pact of the Tome.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
features.summary: At 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level raise one ability by 2 or two abilities by 1 (max 20).

features.name: Mystic Arcanum (6th level)
features.desc:
At 11th level, your patron bestows upon you a magical secret called an arcanum. Choose one 6th- level spell from the warlock spell list as this arcanum.
You can cast your arcanum spell once without expending a spell slot. You must finish a long rest before you can do so again.
At higher levels, you gain more warlock spells of your choice that can be cast in this way: one 7th- level spell at 13th level, one 8th-level spell at 15th level, and one 9th-level spell at 17th level. You regain all uses of your Mystic Arcanum when you finish a long rest.
features.summary: Pick one 6th-level warlock spell as an arcanum; cast it once without using a spell slot, regaining the use on a long rest. Granted first at 11th level.

features.name: Mystic Arcanum (7th level)
features.desc:
At 11th level, your patron bestows upon you a magical secret called an arcanum. Choose one 6th- level spell from the warlock spell list as this arcanum.
You can cast your arcanum spell once without expending a spell slot. You must finish a long rest before you can do so again.
At higher levels, you gain more warlock spells of your choice that can be cast in this way: one 7th- level spell at 13th level, one 8th-level spell at 15th level, and one 9th-level spell at 17th level. You regain all uses of your Mystic Arcanum when you finish a long rest.
features.summary: Pick one 7th-level warlock spell as an arcanum; cast it once without using a spell slot, regaining the use on a long rest.

features.name: Mystic Arcanum (8th level)
features.desc:
At 11th level, your patron bestows upon you a magical secret called an arcanum. Choose one 6th- level spell from the warlock spell list as this arcanum.
You can cast your arcanum spell once without expending a spell slot. You must finish a long rest before you can do so again.
At higher levels, you gain more warlock spells of your choice that can be cast in this way: one 7th- level spell at 13th level, one 8th-level spell at 15th level, and one 9th-level spell at 17th level. You regain all uses of your Mystic Arcanum when you finish a long rest.
features.summary: Pick one 8th-level warlock spell as an arcanum; cast it once without using a spell slot, regaining the use on a long rest.

features.name: Mystic Arcanum (9th level)
features.desc:
At 11th level, your patron bestows upon you a magical secret called an arcanum. Choose one 6th- level spell from the warlock spell list as this arcanum.
You can cast your arcanum spell once without expending a spell slot. You must finish a long rest before you can do so again.
At higher levels, you gain more warlock spells of your choice that can be cast in this way: one 7th- level spell at 13th level, one 8th-level spell at 15th level, and one 9th-level spell at 17th level. You regain all uses of your Mystic Arcanum when you finish a long rest.
features.summary: Pick one 9th-level warlock spell as an arcanum; cast it once without using a spell slot, regaining the use on a long rest.

features.name: Eldritch Master
features.desc:
At 20th level, you can draw on your inner reserve of mystical power while entreating your patron to regain expended spell slots. You can spend 1 minute entreating your patron for aid to regain all your expended spell slots from your Pact Magic feature.
Once you regain spell slots with this feature, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.
features.summary: Spend 1 minute pleading with your patron to recover every expended Pact Magic slot; usable once per long rest.

features.name: Expanded Spell List
features.summary: The Fiend adds its expanded spells (see spells) to the warlock list for you when you learn warlock spells.

features.name: Dark One's Blessing
features.desc: Starting at 1st level, when you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier + your warlock level (minimum of 1).
features.summary: When you drop a hostile creature to 0 HP, gain temporary HP equal to Charisma modifier + warlock level (minimum 1).

features.name: Dark One's Own Luck
features.desc:
Starting at 6th level, you can call on your patron to alter fate in your favor. When you make an ability check or a saving throw, you can use this feature to add a d10 to your roll. You can do so after seeing the initial roll but before any of the roll's effects occur.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
features.summary: Add a d10 to an ability check or saving throw after seeing the roll but before its effects apply.

features.name: Fiendish Resilience
features.desc: Starting at 10th level, you can choose one damage type when you finish a short or long rest. You gain resistance to that damage type until you choose a different one with this feature. Damage from magical weapons or silver weapons ignores this resistance.
features.summary: After a short or long rest pick a damage type to resist until you pick another; magical and silvered weapon damage bypasses it.

features.name: Hurl Through Hell
features.desc:
Starting at 14th level, when you hit a creature with an attack, you can use this feature to instantly transport the target through the lower planes. The creature disappears and hurtles through a nightmare landscape.
At the end of your next turn, the target returns to the space it previously occupied, or the nearest unoccupied space. If the target is not a fiend, it takes 10d10 psychic damage as it reels from its horrific experience.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
features.summary: On a hit, banish the target through the lower planes until the end of your next turn; when it returns, a non-fiend takes 10d10 psychic damage.

features.name: Expanded Spell List
features.summary: The Archfey adds its expanded spells (see spells) to the warlock list for you when you learn warlock spells.

features.name: Fey Presence
features.summary: Action: every creature in a 10-foot cube from you makes a Wisdom save vs your spell DC or is charmed or frightened (your pick) until the end of your next turn.

features.name: Misty Escape
features.summary: Reaction when you take damage: become invisible and teleport up to 60 feet to a visible spot; invisibility lasts until your next turn starts or you attack or cast.

features.name: Beguiling Defenses
features.summary: Immune to being charmed; when someone tries to charm you, your reaction can force a Wisdom save or that creature is charmed by you for 1 minute or until damaged.

features.name: Dark Delirium
features.summary: Action: a creature within 60 feet makes a Wisdom save or is charmed or frightened for up to 1 minute (concentration), lost in an illusory realm; ends if it takes damage.

features.name: Expanded Spell List
features.summary: The Great Old One adds its expanded spells (see spells) to the warlock list for you when you learn warlock spells.

features.name: Awakened Mind
features.summary: Speak telepathically with any creature within 30 feet that knows at least one language, no shared language required.

features.name: Entropic Ward
features.summary: Reaction: impose disadvantage on an attack roll against you; if it misses, you have advantage on your next attack against that creature before the end of your next turn.

features.name: Thought Shield
features.summary: Your mind can't be read unless you allow it; resistance to psychic damage, and creatures that deal psychic damage to you take the same amount.

features.name: Create Thrall
features.summary: Action: touch an incapacitated humanoid to charm it until remove curse, the charm ends, or you use this again; you can talk to it telepathically on the same plane.

choices.name: Beguiling Influence
choices.summary: Gain proficiency in Deception and Persuasion.

choices.name: Bewitching Whispers
choices.summary: Cast compulsion once with a warlock slot; regain on a long rest.

choices.name: Book of Ancient Secrets
choices.summary: Add two 1st-level ritual spells from any class to your Book of Shadows and cast them as rituals; copy more rituals up to half your warlock level (rounded up) at 2 hours and 50 gp per spell level. Also cast known warlock rituals as rituals.

choices.name: Chains of Carceri
choices.summary: Cast hold monster at will on a celestial, fiend, or elemental with no slot or material components; once per creature per long rest.

choices.name: Devil's Sight
choices.summary: See normally in magical and nonmagical darkness out to 120 feet.

choices.name: Dreadful Word
choices.summary: Cast confusion once with a warlock slot; regain on a long rest.

choices.name: Eldritch Sight
choices.summary: Cast detect magic at will without a spell slot.

choices.name: Eldritch Spear
choices.summary: Eldritch blast's range becomes 300 feet.

choices.name: Eyes of the Rune Keeper
choices.summary: You can read any writing.

choices.name: Fiendish Vigor
choices.summary: Cast false life on yourself at will as a 1st-level spell, with no slot or material components.

choices.name: Gaze of Two Minds
choices.summary: Action: touch a willing humanoid and use its senses until the end of your next turn (extendable each turn with an action while on the same plane); you are blind and deaf to your own surroundings meanwhile.

choices.name: Misty Visions
choices.summary: Cast silent image at will with no slot or material components.

choices.name: One with Shadows
choices.summary: In dim light or darkness, use an action to turn invisible until you move or take an action or reaction.

choices.name: Otherworldly Leap
choices.summary: Cast jump on yourself at will with no slot or material components.

choices.name: Repelling Blast
choices.summary: Each eldritch blast hit can shove the target up to 10 feet straight away from you.

choices.name: Sculptor of Flesh
choices.summary: Cast polymorph once with a warlock slot; regain on a long rest.

choices.name: Sign of Ill Omen
choices.summary: Cast bestow curse once with a warlock slot; regain on a long rest.

choices.name: Thief of Five Fates
choices.summary: Cast bane once with a warlock slot; regain on a long rest.

choices.name: Thirsting Blade
choices.summary: Attack twice with your pact weapon when you take the Attack action.

choices.name: Visions of Distant Realms
choices.summary: Cast arcane eye at will without a spell slot.

choices.name: Voice of the Chain Master
choices.summary: Communicate telepathically with your familiar, perceive through its senses, and speak through it in your own voice while on the same plane.

choices.name: Whispers of the Grave
choices.summary: Cast speak with dead at will without a spell slot.

choices.name: Witch Sight
choices.summary: See the true form of shapechangers and of creatures hidden by illusion or transmutation magic within 30 feet and in line of sight.

choices.name: Pact of the Chain
choices.summary: Learn find familiar, cast as a ritual and not counted against spells known; familiar may also be an imp, pseudodragon, quasit, or sprite, and can make one attack when you forgo one of yours during the Attack action.

choices.name: Pact of the Blade
choices.summary: Action: summon a melee pact weapon of any form, proficient and magical for overcoming resistance. Can bind one magic weapon (non-artifact, non-sentient) via a 1-hour ritual to summon instead. Vanishes if more than 5 ft away for 1 minute.

choices.name: Pact of the Tome
choices.summary: Receive a Book of Shadows holding three cantrips from any class list, castable at will while you carry it and not counted against cantrips known; a lost book can be replaced with a 1-hour ceremony.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.desc: As a student of arcane magic, you have a spellbook containing spells that show the first glimmerings of your true power.
features.summary: Intelligence-based prepared casting from a spellbook (starts with six 1st-level spells, +2 free spells per level). Prepare Int mod + wizard level spells after a long rest; ritual-cast spellbook rituals unprepared; arcane focus allowed.

features.name: Arcane Recovery
features.desc:
You have learned to regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. Once per day when you finish a short rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your wizard level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher.
For example, if you're a 4th-level wizard, you can recover up to two levels worth of spell slots. You can recover either a 2nd-level spell slot or two 1st-level spell slots.
features.summary: Once per day after a short rest, recover expended slots whose combined level is at most half your wizard level rounded up; none may be 6th level or higher.

features.name: Arcane Tradition
features.desc:
When you reach 2nd level, you choose an arcane tradition, shaping your practice of magic through one of eight schools, such as Evocation.
Your choice grants you features at 2nd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.
features.summary: Choose one of eight schools (Abjuration, Conjuration, Divination, Enchantment, Evocation, Illusion, Necromancy, Transmutation); it grants features at 2nd, 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
features.summary: At 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level raise one ability by 2 or two abilities by 1 (max 20).

features.name: Spell Mastery
features.desc:
At 18th level, you have achieved such mastery over certain spells that you can cast them at will. Choose a 1st-level wizard spell and a 2nd-level wizard spell that are in your spellbook. You can cast those spells at their lowest level without expending a spell slot when you have them prepared. If you want to cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot as normal.
By spending 8 hours in study, you can exchange one or both of the spells you chose for different spells of the same levels.
features.summary: Pick one 1st-level and one 2nd-level spellbook spell; while prepared, cast them at their base level without a slot. Swap choices with 8 hours of study.

features.name: Signature Spell
features.desc:
When you reach 20th level, you gain mastery over two powerful spells and can cast them with little effort. Choose two 3rd-level wizard spells in your spellbook as your signature spells. You always have these spells prepared, they don't count against the number of spells you have prepared, and you can cast each of them once at 3rd level without expending a spell slot. When you do so, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.
If you want to cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot as normal.
features.summary: (Section heading prints 'Signature Spells'.) Two chosen 3rd-level spellbook spells are always prepared, don't count against prepared spells, and each can be cast once at 3rd level without a slot per short or long rest.

resource.label: Signature spell free casts (one per spell)

features.name: Evocation Savant
features.desc: Beginning when you select this school at 2nd level, the gold and time you must spend to copy an evocation spell into your spellbook is halved.
features.summary: Copying evocation spells into your spellbook costs half the usual gold and time.

features.name: Sculpt Spells
features.desc: Beginning at 2nd level, you can create pockets of relative safety within the effects of your evocation spells. When you cast an evocation spell that affects other creatures that you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 + the spell's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.
features.summary: When casting an evocation spell, choose up to 1 + spell level visible creatures; they automatically succeed on its saves and take no damage where a save would halve it.

features.name: Potent Cantrip
features.desc: Starting at 6th level, your damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect. When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against your cantrip, the creature takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.
features.summary: Creatures that succeed on a save against your cantrip still take half its damage, without other effects.

features.name: Empowered Evocation
features.desc: Beginning at 10th level, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of any wizard evocation spell you cast.
features.summary: Add your Intelligence modifier to the damage roll of wizard evocation spells you cast.

features.name: Overchannel
features.desc:
Starting at 14th level, you can increase the power of your simpler spells. When you cast a wizard spell of 1st through 5th level that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with that spell.
The first time you do so, you suffer no adverse effect. If you use this feature again before you finish a long rest, you take 2d12 necrotic damage for each level of the spell, immediately after you cast it. Each time you use this feature again before finishing a long rest, the necrotic damage per spell level increases by 1d12. This damage ignores resistance and immunity.
features.summary: Deal maximum damage with a damaging wizard spell of 5th level or lower. Free once per long rest; each further use before resting deals you 2d12 necrotic per spell level, +1d12 per level each time, ignoring resistance and immunity.

features.name: Abjuration Savant
features.summary: Copying abjuration spells into your spellbook costs half the usual gold and time.

features.name: Arcane Ward
features.summary: Casting a 1st+ level abjuration spell can create a ward on you (once per long rest) with HP 2 x wizard level + Int mod that absorbs damage to you; later abjuration spells restore 2 x spell level HP to it.

features.name: Projected Ward
features.summary: Reaction: when a creature you can see within 30 feet takes damage, your Arcane Ward absorbs it instead; overflow goes to that creature.

features.name: Improved Abjuration
features.summary: Add your proficiency bonus to ability checks made as part of casting abjuration spells (e.g. counterspell, dispel magic).

features.name: Spell Resistance
features.summary: Advantage on saving throws against spells and resistance to spell damage.

features.name: Conjuration Savant
features.summary: Copying conjuration spells into your spellbook costs half the usual gold and time.

features.name: Minor Conjuration
features.summary: Action: create a nonmagical-looking, faintly glowing object (max 3 ft per side, 10 lb) within 10 feet for 1 hour; ends early if damaged or reused.

features.name: Benign Transposition
features.summary: Action: teleport up to 30 feet, or swap places with a willing Small/Medium creature. Recharges on a long rest or when you cast a 1st+ level conjuration spell.

features.name: Focused Conjuration
features.summary: Taking damage can't break your concentration on a conjuration spell.

features.name: Durable Summons
features.summary: Creatures you summon or create with conjuration spells gain 30 temporary hit points.

features.name: Divination Savant
features.summary: Copying divination spells into your spellbook costs half the usual gold and time.

features.name: Portent
features.summary: After each long rest roll two d20s and keep them; once per turn replace an attack roll, save, or ability check by you or a visible creature with one, decided before rolling. Unused rolls are lost on the next long rest.

features.name: Expert Divination
features.summary: Casting a divination spell of 2nd level or higher with a slot regains one expended slot of a lower level (5th level max).

features.name: The Third Eye
features.summary: Action: gain one chosen sense benefit until incapacitated or you take a short or long rest; reusable after a rest.

features.name: Greater Portent
features.summary: Portent gives you three d20s per long rest instead of two.

choices.summary: See into the Ethereal Plane within 60 feet.

choices.name: Greater Comprehension
choices.summary: Read any language.
